overall: AG found the Advisory Committee violated the OML by not posting notice for its January 9 joint meeting, and the School Committee late-delivered OML materials to Advisory Committee members; location change, certifications, and reading allegations were not violations or were declined.

allegations.summary: The Advisory Committee allegedly failed to post notice for a January 9 joint meeting with the School Committee.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Advisory Committee concedes that it is a public body and that it failed to post notice for its January 9 meeting.

allegations.summary: The School Committee allegedly moved the January 9 meeting location without sufficient public notice after the cafeteria became unavailable.
allegations.key_passage: Where, as here, a public body provides conspicuous and timely signage to indicate to the public that a meeting has been moved within the same building, we do not find an Open Meeting Law violation.

allegations.summary: The School Committee allegedly failed to give Open Meeting Law materials to Advisory Committee members in a timely manner after their appointment.
allegations.key_passage: We also find that the School Committee failed to provide Open Meeting Law materials to all members of the Advisory Committee in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Advisory Committee members allegedly did not certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials.
allegations.key_passage: The Advisory Committee had received certifications from all of its members by the time of its response on February 18 and, therefore, we find that any violation that may have occurred has been remedied.

allegations.summary: Advisory Committee members allegedly failed to read the Open Meeting Law or recent determinations finding violations by the committee.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the School Committee and the Advisory Committee; a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent.
remedy_passage: We order the School Committee’s and Advisory Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
